posts.title: Lombok is Still Relevant in the Age of Java Records
posts.description: Every six months, like clockwork, a new JDK drops—and right on cue, the Java community’s ideological purity tests begin. The usual suspects crawl out to complain about Project Lombok. They argue that it does “weird hacks” to the javac compiler, that it slows down upgrades, and that we don’t need it anymore because we have Records.
